verdict.rationale: Paddle's docs say API keys carry granular permissions that grant access to specific entities or actions, with documented default scopes per endpoint. The MCP docs explicitly recommend least-permission API keys for hard-scoping agents, since the MCP server doesn't gate destructive operations. Live OAuth MCP connections start with read-only access, and sandbox keys (`pdl_sdbx_`) only authenticate against sandbox endpoints, which further limits an agent's blast radius. Missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration that scoped keys work as documented, and detail on how OAuth connector scopes are widened or narrowed beyond the initial read-only access.
